why: freshness scored alpha 0.471 in the first pass; this pilot tests a rewritten decision rule before any re-run
scope: on-topic evidence only (supports majority YES or PARTIAL)
sampling_note: contested rows are oversampled, so the pilot alpha is a LOWER bound on what the rule would score on a straight sample -- that is the point, but do not quote it as a population figure
excerpt_handling: trimmed to the last COMPLETE sentence within the original 700-character window. The source pack cut 98.4% of excerpts at the cap and 77.3% mid-word, which a sentence-aspect rule cannot be applied to. Trimming keeps the excerpt a subset of what the generator saw; median cost 65 characters, no row left without a complete sentence.
new_column: claim_type is collected as a check on the rule: if two raters agree on claim_type but differ on freshness, the labels are wrong; if they differ on claim_type, the rule itself is still ambiguous
target: Krippendorff alpha >= 0.6 on freshness before any re-run
